text: A strong resume opens with a 2-3 line professional summary, followed by experience listed newest first, with each entry written using strong verbs (developed, led, improved) and clear numbers to back up the achievement.
Avoid vague skills like 'good communicator' with no evidence. Write a real situation instead that demonstrates the skill in practice.
If your goal is Machine Learning, the usual path is: solid Python fundamentals, statistics and linear algebra, libraries like NumPy, Pandas and Scikit-learn, then a full hands-on project on GitHub.
For Backend Development, focus on one language well (Python or JavaScript), understand REST APIs, SQL and NoSQL databases, and deployment basics like Docker.
Commonly required NLP skills: text processing (tokenization, embeddings), libraries like Hugging Face Transformers, and a basic understanding of LLMs and RAG.
Recognized certifications in AI: Google's Machine Learning Crash Course, DeepLearning.AI specializations on Coursera, and AWS Certified Machine Learning.
Before any technical interview, review your personal projects well and be ready to explain every technical decision you made and why, not just what you built.
